result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the concept of "otherness"—the artificial divisions that make people see each other as fundamentally different based on race, nationality, religion, gender, or any other arbitrary category. This would dissolve the roots of prejudice, conflict, and inequality, allowing humanity to collaborate without fear or hatred.

The ripple effects would be profound: wars fueled by tribalism would fade, systemic oppression would crumble, and empathy would become the default. People would still have unique identities and cultures, but they wouldn’t be weaponized to justify exclusion or violence.

It’s a simple change in perception, but it would rewrite the rules of human interaction. The world wouldn’t be perfect—greed, ego, and misunderstanding would persist—but it would be a foundation for something far more just and connected.
